question: Does the calibrated excess-error monitor and unchanged wrong-first/revert/correct-retain policy generalize without retuning across fresh immutable real-byte files and four heterogeneous level-1 motif-state degradation classes?
hypothesis: Across two fresh immutable held-out blobs and four preregistered motif-state degradation classes per file, the unchanged calibrated excess-error monitor will identify the damaged motif in all 8 sequential cycles, every wrong same-budget repair will be rejected/reverted, every exact canonical repair will exceed the unchanged 0.20 selected-key validation-gain threshold and be retained, and independent audit will restore exact canonical predictions, probabilities, and 256-motif structure after every cycle.
authority: research-only immutable real-byte maintenance generalization; no deployment, external-model inference, scheduler, queue, broker, accepted-ref, runtime, or capacity authority changes

canonical_training.construction: exact WLM-LM-REAL-UTF8-BYTE-PILOT-R2 four training Git blobs and byte-identical TrainModel path

fresh_evaluation_blobs.selection_basis: largest currently available docs/experiments file not used by the supported real-byte pilot
largest currently available unitary Go source not used by the supported real-byte pilot

evaluation_segmentation: Each fresh blob is divided by raw byte index into four contiguous non-overlapping quarters: pre-degradation calibration, diagnostic monitor, candidate validation, final audit. Context resets at quarter boundaries.

calibrated_monitor.background: For each canonical selected motif, calibration-quarter occurrence/error counts under canonical model.
calibrated_monitor.diagnostic: For each canonical retained key, diagnostic-quarter occurrence/error counts under current active model.
calibrated_monitor.selection: highest excess-error score; lexicographic raw-key tie break

eligibility: key is one of the frozen 256 canonical selected motifs
canonical motif top-1 accuracy minus baseline top-1 accuracy on calibration occurrences >=0.20
applying that class on calibration occurrences lowers selected-key top-1 accuracy by >=0.20
target_schedule.ordering: For each class in frozen class order, among eligible not-yet-used keys choose highest calibration occurrence, then highest canonical-over-baseline calibration gain, then lexicographic raw four-byte key.
target_schedule.hidden_from_policy: class identity, scheduled target key, schedule rank, calibration gains, and evaluator class-sensitivity checks

degradation_classes.record_missing: delete the selected motif record from active map
degradation_classes.successor_distribution_rotated: preserve selected key and total count but rotate the canonical 256 successor-count buckets by +1 byte; recompute best/bestCount/consistency
degradation_classes.canonical_best_bucket_erased: preserve selected key; set only the canonical best-successor count to zero; recompute total/best/bestCount/consistency
degradation_classes.nonzero_counts_flattened: preserve selected key; replace every positive canonical successor count with 1 and every zero count with 0; recompute total/best/bestCount/consistency

sequential_state: Every cycle starts from the retained repaired state of the previous cycle. After successful audit, active state must equal canonical exactly before the next heterogeneous degradation is applied.

candidates.retained_catalog: bounded canonical copy of the 256 selected motif records
candidates.wrong_first: lexicographically next retained key whose canonical best successor differs; install its full 256-count distribution under monitor-selected raw key
candidates.correct_second: install monitor-selected key's own retained canonical record

validation_policy.selected_key_metric: top-1 accuracy on validation-quarter occurrences of monitor-selected raw key
validation_policy.global_metric: Jeffreys-smoothed overall bits-per-byte using the supported real-byte probability rule
validation_policy.retain_rule: retain iff selected-key accuracy gain versus degraded pre-candidate state >=0.20 AND global bits-per-byte change <=0.005; otherwise exact revert
validation_policy.candidate_order: wrong first; exact revert if rejected; correct second

final_audit: active key set exactly equals canonical 256-key set
every active motif successor-count array, total, best, bestCount, and consistency exactly equal canonical
adaptive top-1 prediction at every audit next-byte position equals canonical model
adaptive smoothed probability for every observed audit target equals canonical model
validity_criteria: Exact parent, North Star, supported calibrated-maintenance evidence identity, training blob identities, and fresh evaluation blob identities match.
Fresh evaluation blobs are absent from all supported-pilot training/evaluation sets.
Exactly four distinct scheduled targets per file are selected before diagnostic execution by the frozen class-specific evaluator eligibility/order.
Calibration, diagnostic, validation, and audit quarters are byte-disjoint and context resets at each boundary.
The deployed monitor algorithm and score are byte-identical to supported calibrated maintenance and receive no class label or target identity.
Each degradation modifies only the selected motif record according to the frozen class rule; all other model state is unchanged.
Wrong/correct candidate budget and ordering are unchanged from supported calibrated maintenance.
Every rejected wrong candidate restores exact pre-candidate degraded state; every retained correct state becomes the next cycle start.
No tokenizer, evaluator schedule, class/lesion label, canonical diagnostic shadow, external model, capacity growth, retraining, or post-result threshold change is used.
Full Go regression passes before probe execution and normalized result carries exact experiment identity.

classification_rules.supported: All validity criteria and all frozen thresholds pass across all 8 cycles and all four degradation classes.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes and correct repairs recover exact audit state, but at least one monitor-separation, wrong-candidate, per-class, validation, or budget threshold fails.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but calibrated monitoring, wrong-candidate rejection, correct retention, or exact audit restoration fails for one or more degradation classes.
classification_rules.incomplete: Fresh blob support or compute interruption prevents the complete 8-cycle matrix.
classification_rules.invalid: Blob identity, train/eval isolation, target/class schedule isolation, quarter isolation, degradation construction, candidate parity, revert semantics, deterministic construction, capacity, or qualification criteria fail.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter fresh blobs, quarter split, class set/order, class-specific eligibility, calibrated monitor, candidate construction/order, validation rule, budgets, metrics, thresholds, aggregation, or classification after any experiment output is observed.
